messages:
marie: Heads-up: ran nsys on the /generate hot path with KV cache prefetch enabled. Trace shows a long H2D cudaMemcpyAsync on stream 3 that overlaps compute on stream 0 and creates 5-10ms tail latency spikes. perfetto link: https://perfetto.example/trace/2311112222 - snapshot in the thread below.
ryan: Can you paste the nsys timeline / kernel names you saw?
marie: Sure — short excerpt from the timeline view:
```
Stream 0: conv_fwd_v2_kernel       0.28 ms  (compute)
Stream 3: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D    8.52 ms  (host->device pinned)
Stream 0: attention_kv_update     queued while memcpy active
CPU(12): hostspin -> sched_wakeup after memcpy completes
```
devon: That memcpy looks like KV prefetch spilling whole layer shards. We currently prefetch layer chunks when batcher heuristic sees seq_len > 2048. Might be too large for this machine.
marie: Exactly. nsys shows stream 3 copies dominate the timeline and kernels on stream 0 get queued until the hostcopy finishes, even though they are on different streams. There's also a pattern of CPU preemption / hostspin around the wakeup.
tara: Which instance/OS/kernel were these runs on? Could be scheduler latency on the host delaying the GPU work submit.
marie: g4dn.12xlarge-like node, Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15.9. Perf trace correlates `sched_wakeup` and `futex` activity from the batching thread immediately after the memcpy returns.
nsys-bot: Trace analysis summary: 1) High H2D occupancy on stream 3. 2) Default stream priorities: copy stream lower than compute stream -> but GPU-side serialization visible. 3) Host thread wake path adds ~1-3ms on some samples. Suggested mitigations: use stream priorities, split prefetch into smaller chunks, or move to pinned page-locked buffers with streaming.
ryan: We tried stream priorities in the past but the batcher increases prefetch size as it aggregates microbatches -> larger contiguous copies. Could try chunking logic: if batch_size >= 8 then prefetch in N chunks of ~4MB.
devon: Also evaluate cudaHostAlloc with portable or mapped flags vs cudaMalloc+cudaMemcpyAsync. Mapped memory can reduce copies but may affect throughput for large transfers.
marie: Proposed action plan:
- repro locally with nsys+perfetto sampling and a microbench that simulates the same batcher prefetch sizes.
- add a `KVCACHE_PREFETCH_CHUNK_MB` runtime opt in dev branch to split prefetch.
- instrument telemetry for memcpy durations and CPU wake latency.
- run A/B on a small dedicated pool.
Does that sound reasonable?
tara: Yes. Also capture kernel names + stream ids in telemetry so we can correlate which kernels are most affected. Add an opt to disable eager prefetch for seq_len > X.
ryan: I'll open a small PR with chunking and a perf microbenchmark. Will post results as soon as I have perf numbers (aiming for a ~10% tail latency drop). :thumbsup:
marie: Thanks — I'll attach the perfetto/hsys traces to the PR. main perf link: https://perfetto.example/trace/2311112222 and nsys export: s3://redwood-traces/2311112222/nsys.zip
nsys-bot: Note: if you re-run with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu` you'll get better CPU wake correlation.
ryan: 👍 running that now on a repro harness, will update thread.
marie: tagging @eng-sre to watch the dedicated pool job once we roll this out for A/B.
